questions.stem: The anatomical reference position is the position on which all anatomical descriptions are based. Which of the following correspond to this anatomical reference position?
options: A living adult, seated
Arms hanging along the body
Palms of the hands facing inward
Gaze directed upward
Feet together, placed on the ground

questions.stem: The Nomina Anatomica is an essential basis for communication between physicians and scientists. Which of the following correspond to the Nomina Anatomica?
options: It is written in English
It is written in Latin
It is a European nomenclature
It is an international nomenclature
It universalizes the study of the human body

questions.stem: For descriptive, topographic and functional anatomy, we use reference axes: the body axis, the hand axis and the foot axis. What are the characteristics of the foot axis?
options: A longitudinal axis
A transverse axis
An axis passing through the 4th toe
An axis passing through the 3rd toe
An axis passing through the 2nd toe

questions.stem: During the Muslim renaissance, several scientists marked this period. Who is the founder of modern optics and the first scientist to describe the anatomy of the eye?
options: Ibn Rushd
Ibn Al-Haytham
Ibn Nafis
Abu Al-Qasim Al-Zahrawi
Ibn Sina

questions.stem: Medial rotation is a rotational movement from outside to inside. What are its axis and plane?
options: A transverse axis and a sagittal plane
A sagittal axis and a frontal plane
A vertical axis and a transverse plane
A vertical axis and a sagittal plane
A transverse axis and a frontal plane

questions.stem: Cartilage is a specialized connective tissue; it is elastic and resistant. Which of the following correspond to hyaline cartilage?
options: A bluish cartilage
A whitish cartilage
A yellowish cartilage
A glassy (vitreous) cartilage
A translucent cartilage

questions.stem: Bone growth is of two types: growth in length and growth in width. Which structure is responsible for growth in width?
options: The epiphyseal cartilage (growth plate)
The articular cartilage
Compact bone
The periosteum
Spongy bone

questions.stem: Morphologically, the bone surface is not regular; it shows reliefs and cavities. Which of the following correspond to non-articular eminences?
options: A crest
A foramen
A process
A spine
A groove (sulcus)

questions.stem: The femur is a long bone forming the skeleton of the thigh. It has a proximal epiphysis, a distal epiphysis and a diaphysis. What are the articular surfaces of the distal epiphysis?
options: The medial epicondyle of the femur
The patellar surface of the femur
The medial condyle
The lateral condyle
The posterior surface of the patella

questions.stem: The hip bone (os coxae) is a flat, twisted bone shaped like a two-bladed propeller. It connects the lower limb to the spine. Which of the following belong to its lateral surface?
options: The posterior gluteal line
The obturator foramen
The arcuate line
The auricular surface
The acetabulum

questions.stem: The hip bone has 4 borders: superior, inferior, anterior and posterior. Which of the following belong to its anterior border?
options: The innominate notch
The greater sciatic notch
The iliopectineal (iliopubic) eminence
The lesser innominate notch
The ischial tuberosity

questions.stem: The tibial plateau articulates with the femoral condyles. Which anatomical elements make it up?
options: The fibular articular surface
The anterior intercondylar area
The oblique crest
The intercondylar tubercles
The medial malleolus

questions.stem: The tarsal bones of the foot are seven, arranged in an anterior tarsus and a posterior tarsus. Which are the bones of the anterior tarsus?
options: Lunate
The cuboid
The talus
The calcaneus
The navicular

questions.stem: The femur has a sharp posterior border (the linea aspera) which gives attachment to several hip and thigh muscles. Which of the following muscles attach to this border?
options: The gluteus medius
The adductor muscles of the thigh
The vastus medialis
The vastus lateralis
The obturator externus

questions.stem: The articular capsule of the knee is a fibrous sleeve connecting the articular surfaces, inserting more or less close to the articular cartilage. What are its characteristics?
options: It thickens posteriorly to form the condylar shells (caps)
It thickens anteriorly to form the condylar shells (caps)
It has an anterior window for the patella
It has an anterior window for the fabella
It has a posterior window for the fabella

questions.stem: The knee joint is a weight-bearing joint with a ligamentous and tendinous system providing stability when standing and walking. The collateral system is a powerful ligament of this joint. What are its characteristics?
options: It is formed by the cruciate ligaments
It is formed by the collateral ligaments
Its injury produces a drawer movement
It ensures antero-posterior stability of the knee
It ensures lateral (collateral) stability of the knee

questions.stem: Knee flexion brings the posterior surface of the leg toward the posterior surface of the thigh. What is the range of active flexion with the hip extended?
According to their anatomical structure and mobility, there are three types of joints. Among them, syndesmoses are:
options: Fibrous joints whose articular surfaces are covered with articular cartilage
Fibrous joints that unite the teeth to their sockets
Joined by fibrocartilaginous structures
Joints between articular surfaces that are distant from each other
Fibrous joints that progressively ossify over time

questions.stem: According to the morphology of the articular surfaces, six types of joints are distinguished. Ginglymus (hinge) joints:
options: Unite two articular surfaces, one concave and the other convex
Unite two pulley-shaped articular surfaces
Have a single axis of movement
Are also called condylar joints
Are amphiarthrosis-type joints

questions.stem: Synovial joints have great mobility. Adduction:
options: Is a movement performed around a transverse axis
Is a movement that carries the anterior surface of a segment outward
Is a simple movement performed by a single type of joint
Is a movement specific to spheroid joints
Is a movement performed in a frontal plane

questions.stem: The scapula is a thin, flat, asymmetric bone located on the postero-superior part of the thorax:
options: The pillar of the scapula is a vertical ridge that delimits its dorsal surface
Its cervical (superior) border shows the coracoid notch medially
Its lateral border is the longest and thickest
The glenoid cavity is carried by the neck of the scapula
The tip (inferior angle) of the scapula lies opposite the 8th rib

questions.stem: The clavicle is a long bone that forms the shoulder girdle with the scapula:
options: Its caudal (inferior) surface has the costal tuberosity on its medial part
The conoid tubercle is located laterally and anteriorly on the ventral surface
The trapezoid ligament attaches to the ventral tubercle of its caudal surface
Its cranial (superior) surface gives attachment to the costoclavicular ligament
Its anterior border is concave in its medial part

questions.stem: The humerus is a long bone forming the skeleton of the arm. It articulates above with the scapula and below with the two forearm bones:
options: The radial nerve groove on its dorsal surface is oblique downward and outward
The bicipital groove extends its antero-lateral surface downward
Its proximal epiphysis is entirely articular
The distal epiphysis articulates only with the ulna
The trochlea occupies the medial part of the humeral condyle

questions.stem: The radius is a long bone of the forearm occupying its lateral part:
options: The fovea of the radial head articulates with the medial part of the humeral condyle
The radial tuberosity gives attachment to the biceps brachii
The medial surface of its distal end extends downward as the styloid process
The inferior surface of its distal end articulates with the first row of the carpus
Its proximal epiphysis has a single articular surface

questions.stem: The scapulohumeral (glenohumeral) joint is the main shoulder joint; it unites the humeral head to the glenoid cavity of the scapula:
options: It is a deep, fragile and very mobile joint
It is a diarthrosis of the enarthrosis (ball-and-socket) type
It is a mobile joint with two degrees of freedom
Adduction is possible on its own
Flexion is a movement in the sagittal plane, also called antepulsion

questions.stem: The glenoid labrum is a fibrocartilaginous ring applied around the rim of the glenoid cavity:
options: Its peripheral surface is free, smooth and convex
Its external surface is covered with articular cartilage
Its internal surface extends outward the surface of the scapular neck
It is richly innervated and vascularized
Its lesions heal spontaneously

questions.stem: The sterno-costo-clavicular joint is a true joint of the shoulder complex:
options: It is a plane joint of the arthrodial type
It is a synovial joint with an intermediate articular disc
It unites two articular surfaces
It allows very slight gliding movements
It allows two types of movements

questions.stem: The subtalar joint is one of the joints of the foot:
options: It is the joint uniting the posterior tarsus to the anterior tarsus
It is a synovial joint of the spheroid type
It unites the posterior calcaneal surface to the posterior talar surface
It has a capsule and two passive ligaments
It is a mobile joint with two degrees of freedom

questions.stem: The ankle joint unites the two leg bones to the talus and is of the trochlear type:
options: The tibiofibular mortise has a medial wall facing the lateral surface of the talus
The tibiofibular mortise has three walls, the superior one being fibular
The tibial plafond (pilon) faces the talar trochlea
The medial collateral ligament is made of two bundles, anterior and posterior
The posterior bundle of the fibular collateral ligament extends from the lateral malleolus to the posterior surface of the talus

questions.stem: The ulna is a long bone of the forearm forming the medial part of the forearm skeleton:
options: The posterior surface of the olecranon is triangular with a concave inferior base
The ulnar tuberosity marks the antero-inferior surface of the coronoid process
The ulnar head has a single articular surface
The anterior surface of the olecranon and the superior surface of the coronoid process form the trochlear notch of the ulna
The beak of the olecranon extends its medial surface

questions.stem: The radio-ulnar articular disc:
options: Is a fibrocartilaginous structure
Is triangular in shape
Occupies the medial 2/3 of the antebrachial articular surface
Is interposed between the ulna and the radius
Articulates with the triquetrum and the pisiform

questions.stem: The trapeziometacarpal joint:
options: Is one of the intercarpal joints
Unites the trapezium and the head of metacarpal I
Is a saddle-type synovial joint
Is very mobile
Performs rotational movements of the thumb

questions.stem: The internal surface of the annular ligament of the radius:
options: Is purely fibrous in structure
Is covered with cartilage
Attaches anteriorly to the anterior border of the radial notch of the ulna
Encircles the radial head
Articulates with the articular circumference of the radius

questions.stem: Which passive ligament of the elbow joint attaches to the radius?
options: The ulnar collateral ligament of the elbow
The radial collateral ligament of the elbow
The oblique ligament of the elbow
The posterior ligament
The quadrate ligament

questions.stem: The elbow joint performs the following movements:
options: Flexion, with a range of 140° to 160°
Extension, with a range of 0°
Pronation, with a range of 85°
Supination, with a range of 80°
Circumduction

questions.stem: The pubofemoral ligament:
options: Attaches to the ischial tuberosity
Attaches to the iliopectineal (iliopubic) eminence
Was formerly called the ligament of Bertin
Is an intrasynovial ligament
Is an active ligament

questions.stem: The ligament of the head of the femur:
options: Was formerly called the round ligament of the femoral head
Plays a role in nourishing the femoral head
Is an intrasynovial and intracapsular ligament
Reinforces the articular capsule
Attaches at the fovea capitis

questions.stem: The acetabulum:
options: Is the only articular surface of the hip bone
Is surrounded by the glenoid labrum
Is surrounded by the cotyloid (acetabular) labrum
Is entirely covered with articular cartilage
Is partially covered with articular cartilage

questions.stem: Muscle has the following properties:
options: Tonicity
Rigidity
Elasticity
Contractility
Excitability

questions.stem: The roles of muscles are:
options: Heat production
Vitamin production
Production of movement
Concentration of clotting factors
Stabilization of joints
